# Vendored third-party code

Other authors' code, vendored in-tree — there is no package manager — and compiled into **both** app targets: `taglib/`, `PINCache/`, `PINOperation/`, `r8brain/`. **Do not restyle it.** Adding or removing a file means editing `project.yml` and re-running `xcodegen generate`.

Every component must be listed in `THIRD-PARTY-NOTICES.md` at the repo root with the license it is used under. **TagLib is dual-licensed (LGPL 2.1 or MPL 1.1) and Vibe elects MPL 1.1** — that election is load-bearing, because TagLib is statically compiled into the app and the LGPL's static-linking obligation is incompatible with App Store distribution. Read that file before touching `taglib/`.

- **taglib** (a subset of TagLib 2.2) extracts audio metadata. Only the formats the app plays are vendored: `mpeg/` and ID3, `mp4/`, `flac/`, `riff/`, plus the APE *tag* machinery MPEG files need and `ogg/xiphcomment` for FLAC comments. `TagLib::FileRef` is deliberately unused, since its detection references every format parser; `AudioTrackMetadata.mm` has a `TagLibAudioFile` factory that mirrors FileRef's extension-then-content-sniff detection for the supported formats. When updating, re-copy the subset and let the linker report anything new.
- **PINCache** and **PINOperation** provide disk and memory caching for metadata and waveform data. `PINDiskCache.m` is excluded from the recursive `ThirdParty` entry and re-added with a per-file `-fobjc-arc-exceptions` flag, as the pod's ARC-exception-safe subspec did. `make check-layout` whitelists that exclude, along with the `.xcprivacy`, `.txt` and `LICENSE.MPL` ones that keep license and privacy files out of the bundle — this directory is the only place file-level excludes are allowed at all.

- **r8brain** (r8brain-free-src, upstream commit `9e73d2dd`) is the voice bus's resampler (`Audio/AudioResampler.mm`). It is header-only apart from the two files `project.yml` excludes and re-adds with their own flags, `DLL/r8bsrc.cpp` (upstream's C entry points, where every template is instantiated) and `fft/pffft_double.c`: `-O3` in every configuration, since at `-O0` it would cost many times its optimized self and a Debug build is where its quality and cost tests run; `-DR8BSRC_DECL=` (upstream's switch from a DLL to an object file); `R8B_PFFFT_DOUBLE`, the README's speed setting (double-precision PFFFT at Ooura's accuracy) — its other, `R8B_EXTFFT`, costs more than it saves at the 1% transition band `Audio/AudioResampler.mm` uses, so it is off (`docs/audio-quality.md`); and `PFFFT_ENABLE_NEON`. **TRAP: PFFFT's NEON path is opt-in, and `-w` hides the `#pragma message` that says so** — without the macro arm64 builds PFFFT's scalar fallback, 15–20% slower, with no error; x86_64 picks SSE2 by itself. Check with `clang -arch arm64 -fsyntax-only fft/pffft_double.c` plus the flags, which prints the backend chosen. `-w` silences the vendored C's warnings. Every file that includes an r8brain header must see the same `R8B_*` macros, so nothing but `r8bsrc.cpp` includes them. Upstream's `LICENSE` is vendored as `LICENSE.txt`, and the `.inc` filter tables are excluded, so neither is bundled. Only what those two files compile is vendored (checked with `clang -H` for arm64 and x86_64): not upstream's `r8butil.h`, the single-precision `pffft.c`, the Ooura `fft4g.h` (unused under `R8B_PFFFT_DOUBLE`), the Windows DLL builds, `bench/` or `other/`. When updating, re-copy the same set and re-run that check.

`ThirdParty/` is excluded from `make analyze` and from every other check in the repo, on the same grounds: it is not ours to fix.

Framework-style imports such as `<PINCache/...>` resolve through the shared `vibe-header-paths` setting group in `project.yml`, which both app targets use so a second platform cannot drift from the first.
